summary:
Missions to the lunar South Pole and far side face extreme lighting, terrain, and communication constraints. The Lunar Landing Site & CLPS Mission Navigator is an interactive web application designed to bridge science and engineering data for lunar surface exploration. 

Our tool combines a multi-parameter mission browser with an interactive selenographic hologram map displaying real landing coordinates from the North Pole to the South Pole. Users can search and filter missions by commercial provider, launch year, status, landing site, or NASA scientific payload. Clicking on any landing pin or mission card opens a comprehensive telemetry inspector that integrates solar and Earth elevation angles from the NASA JPL Horizons System to evaluate solar power generation and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows. Additionally, each site profile incorporates terrain slope and horizon mask summaries derived from LRO Quickmap and NASA Moon Trek, alongside international Artemis context from the CSA Moon Exploration portal.
details:
What it does & How it works:

Lunar Landing Site & CLPS Mission Navigator is a client-side web platform built with React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. It provides an intuitive interface for exploring NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) deliveries and candidate polar landing regions:

1. Interactive Selenographic Hologram Map: Plots landing site coordinates across the lunar globe with real-time filtering and interactive telemetry pins.

2. Solar & Earth Ephemeris Assessments: Displays local Sun and Earth elevation angles above the horizon (derived from JPL Horizons System data) to assess solar array illumination and Direct-to-Earth radio communication constraints.

3. Topographic & Horizon Profiles: Summarizes local crater slopes, boulder hazards, and horizon elevation masks using LRO Quickmap and Moon Trek 3D datasets.

4. Payload & Vendor Directory: Catalogs NASA science instruments and international partner contributions across completed, active, and planned missions.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

By unifying mission manifests, surface topography, and ephemeris constraints into a single visual dashboard, our project makes complex lunar mission planning accessible to students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

Tools & Coding Languages Used:

- Frontend: JavaScript (ES6+), React 18, Tailwind CSS, HTML5, SVG graphics

- Build Tooling: Vite, Node.js, Git & GitHub
